en.seoTitle: Codex — Agent Workflow Design Guide | Floatboat
en.description: Study Codex’s open agent harness to improve your own workflows: connect tools to task context, carry state across steps, and define review boundaries. Use its runtime and integration design as a reference for work in Floatboat.
overview: Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent and open agent harness. The public project provides the surrounding execution system: it helps an agent inspect a workspace, maintain a conversation, use tools, and carry a task through successive steps. The harness is the software around a model, rather than the model weights.

For a Floatboat user, the useful question is which part of a workflow needs a stronger execution loop. Codex offers a concrete reference for connecting task context, tools, feedback, and human approval. Reusing its software is one option; applying these design principles to an existing workflow is another.

The repository uses Apache-2.0. OpenAI’s models, subscriptions, and managed services have their own access and commercial terms. Publishing the harness makes its implementation inspectable; it does not promise that every hosted Codex feature is included in a local checkout.

faq.question: Is Codex a model or an agent harness?
faq.answer: The open-source Codex project is an agent and harness implementation. It organizes context, tools, and task execution around model calls. The models it can access are a separate part of the system.

faq.question: How do the CLI, SDK, and app-server differ?
faq.answer: The CLI is a direct interactive interface. The SDK supports programmatic agent workflows, while app-server exposes a session protocol for applications that need ongoing conversations, events, and approval handling.

faq.question: Does the source include free model access?
faq.answer: No. Apache-2.0 covers the project source. Model access, subscription entitlements, API usage, and managed services follow their own terms and can have separate charges or limits.

faq.question: Can Codex be built into a different interface?
faq.answer: OpenAI documents app-server and SDK integration for that purpose. The application supplies its own interface and relevant context, and should define what tools the agent can use and which actions need review.

faq.question: Does an open harness include every hosted feature?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The public runtime and integration surfaces are distinct from hosted infrastructure, account features, and model services. Verify the particular feature in its official documentation.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Codex as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

en.description: Use DeepSeek Harness as a reference for composing your own agent workflows. Study its plugin architecture to separate model access, tools, and task capabilities, then evaluate focused extensions for work organized in Floatboat.
overview: DeepSeek Harness, also called dsh, is an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek. It provides a runtime around model interaction rather than a new model in itself. The project’s central design is to express the system through composable plugins.

Its value for workflow design is the separation of capabilities into composable parts. A Floatboat user can use that idea to identify the tools, context, and responsibilities a task requires before considering a specific plugin or runtime integration. The reference architecture does not establish a ready-made connection to Floatboat.

DeepSeek describes the project as a developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes expected. Its MIT source license is separate from model-provider access and third-party dependencies. Evaluate it as an evolving platform, with version-specific documentation and deliberate workspace boundaries.

faq.question: Is DeepSeek Harness an official DeepSeek project?
faq.answer: Yes. It is published in the deepseek-ai organization, and its README explicitly identifies DeepSeek AI as the developer. Use that repository rather than assuming a similarly named community fork is official.

faq.question: What does everything-is-a-plugin mean here?
faq.answer: It describes the project’s Cordis-based composition model. The runtime’s capabilities are assembled through plugins; the actual tools and behavior still depend on the plugins and configuration selected for a session.

faq.question: Is dsh a separate AI model?
faq.answer: No. dsh is the runtime and application entry point. Model inference comes from the provider configured for the session, with that provider’s own credentials, availability, and commercial terms.

faq.question: How stable is the project interface?
faq.answer: The official README marks it as a developer preview and explicitly expects compatibility-breaking changes. Pin and evaluate the version you use instead of assuming an extension will work unchanged across releases.

faq.question: Does MIT cover connected models and services?
faq.answer: MIT applies to the project source. Model APIs, external services, and third-party components retain their own terms, costs, and operational requirements.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use DeepSeek Harness as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

en.description: Explore DeepSeek’s research prototype for turning authorized GitHub and Feishu requests into coding tasks. Study task routing, scoped execution, and reviewable delivery for your own agent workflows.
overview: DSH Superagent Prototype is a proactive coding agent published in DeepSeek’s official GitHub organization. It runs as a DeepSeek Harness bundle for one GitHub repository, with optional Feishu input. Authorized requests become tasks that execute in their own sessions and working directories, then return results to the original conversation.

Its useful workflow patterns include evaluating incoming requests, keeping each task within an assigned scope, and following discussion without treating every message as new authority. The web panel prioritizes work needing a person and also exposes history and operational health.

The MIT-licensed repository is research code, explicitly described as not an official DeepSeek product or production-ready software. Its published implementation differs from the internal version and the accompanying design article; some ideas discussed there remain unimplemented.

faq.question: Is DSH Superagent a DeepSeek model?
faq.answer: It is agent application code running on DeepSeek Harness. A separately configured model provider supplies inference; the project itself is not model weights or a model API subscription.

faq.question: How does it differ from DeepSeek Harness?
faq.answer: Harness provides the surrounding agent runtime and extension system. Superagent is a bundle built on that runtime to coordinate requests, tasks, sessions, and delivery for a repository.

faq.question: Does it need Feishu or support every GitHub deployment?
faq.answer: Feishu is optional. The documented scope is one github.com repository per deployment; GitHub Enterprise Server is unsupported. The agent needs a dedicated GitHub user with write access, rather than a GitHub App.

faq.question: Does observe mode stop every task from running?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates inferred candidates and records positive assessments without accepting them. Explicit requests work in every mode; automatic acceptance of inferred work requires auto mode and matching rules.

faq.question: Are workers isolated from the rest of my computer?
faq.answer: No security sandbox is provided by the separate task directories or account wrappers. The documented presets run with full OS-user access, so the deployment guide recommends a dedicated OS account containing only the agent credentials.

faq.question: Does MIT make it production-ready or include free inference?
faq.answer: MIT covers the source code. Model services and machine operation have separate costs and terms. The README identifies the software as a research prototype, with differences from its internal implementation and some unimplemented design ideas.

faq.question: DSH Superagent 是 DeepSeek 模型吗？
faq.answer: 它是在 DeepSeek Harness 上运行的 Agent 应用代码，推理由另行配置的模型服务提供。项目本身不是模型权重，也不包含模型 API 订阅。

faq.question: 它与 DeepSeek Harness 有什么区别？
faq.answer: Harness 提供 Agent 运行环境与扩展机制；Superagent 是基于它构建的扩展包，负责仓库中的请求接收、任务管理、会话执行与结果交付。

faq.question: 必须接入飞书吗，支持所有 GitHub 环境吗？
faq.answer: 飞书是可选入口。当前文档限定一次部署面向一个 github.com 仓库，不支持 GitHub Enterprise Server。执行身份需要具有仓库写权限的专用 GitHub 用户账号，而非 GitHub App。

faq.question: observe 模式会阻止全部任务执行吗？
faq.answer: 不会。它会评估推断任务，并记录本来会接受的结果，但不真正接受这些任务。显式请求在所有模式下仍可执行；推断任务自动接受需要启用 auto 模式并匹配规则。

faq.question: 独立工作目录能隔离我的电脑吗？
faq.answer: 不能。独立任务目录和账号包装不构成安全沙箱。文档中的预设拥有操作系统用户的完整执行权限，因此部署指南建议使用只放置 Agent 凭据的专用操作系统账号。

faq.question: MIT 是否意味着已经成熟并且推理免费？

en.seoTitle: Pi — Agent Workflow Design Guide | Floatboat
en.description: Study Pi’s minimal agent core, extension packages, and reusable libraries to shape your own workflows. Compare where task instructions are enough, where runtime customization helps, and which execution boundaries your environment must provide.
overview: Pi explicitly describes itself as a minimal, extensible agent harness. The project combines an interactive coding agent with supporting libraries for model access, agent execution, conversation state, and terminal interfaces. It is both a usable tool and a collection of building blocks.

Pi is useful when designing a workflow that needs a small core with selective additions. In Floatboat-related work, use it to distinguish a reusable task instruction from a new tool or runtime behavior. Some improvements only need better Skills; others justify evaluating an extension or library.

The current repository is earendil-works/pi, following the earlier badlogic/pi-mono location, and uses MIT. Pi also explicitly says it has no built-in permission system restricting filesystem, process, network, or credential access. Hosting it safely requires the surrounding environment to provide the boundaries you need.

faq.question: Is Pi officially described as a harness?
faq.answer: Yes. The README explicitly calls Pi a minimal, extensible agent harness. It also contains a coding CLI and reusable libraries, so the repository covers more than one user-facing interface.

faq.question: Why do old links use badlogic/pi-mono?
faq.answer: That was the earlier repository address. It currently redirects to earendil-works/pi. Use the current upstream for ownership and documentation, and check older package references before reusing them.

faq.question: Does Pi include a built-in permission sandbox?
faq.answer: The README says Pi has no built-in permission system for restricting filesystem, process, network, or credential access. Required containment must come from the environment, not from an assumption that every harness provides it.

faq.question: Are subagents and plan mode enabled by default?
faq.answer: The project deliberately leaves those features out of its core defaults. Extensions or packages may supply them, but their presence and behavior must be checked for the particular setup.

faq.question: What is the difference between a Skill and an extension?
faq.answer: A Skill supplies reusable task instructions and resources. An extension changes or extends the running tool through the extension mechanism. They can work together, but their execution and trust boundaries differ.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Pi as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

faq.answer: 是。README 明确将 Pi 称为精简、可扩展的 Agent Harness，同时提供编程 CLI 和可复用基础库，范围不止一个终端界面。

faq.question: Pi 是否自带权限沙箱？
faq.answer: README 说明 Pi 没有用于限制文件、进程、网络和凭证访问的内置权限系统。需要的隔离应由环境提供，不能假定所有 harness 都自带沙箱。

faq.question: 子 Agent 和规划模式默认就有吗？
faq.answer: 项目有意不将这类能力作为核心默认功能。扩展或包可以补充，是否可用取决于所选扩展、包和会话配置。

faq.question: Skill 与扩展在 Pi 中有什么区别？
faq.answer: Skill 提供可复用的任务说明与资料，扩展则通过扩展机制改变或增加工具行为。两者可以配合，但执行方式与信任边界不同。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？

en.seoTitle: OpenCode — Agent Workflow Design Guide | Floatboat
en.description: Study OpenCode’s coding-agent workflow to improve how your own tasks move from investigation to changes and review. Use its interaction and extension design as references for development work organized in Floatboat.
overview: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent published by Anomaly. It connects task conversations with repository tools. The model service supplies reasoning and generation, the execution environment handles files and commands, and the application coordinates the workflow.

For workflow design, OpenCode is a concrete implementation to study rather than a requirement to switch products. Its agent modes and interactive feedback can inform how you separate investigation from implementation, expose a change for review, and add task-specific integrations to your own environment.

The project source is MIT licensed. Model-provider accounts, subscription access, remote services, and community additions have separate requirements. The source can be inspected and adapted without implying that all associated hosted services are free or included.

faq.question: Is OpenCode a model provider?
faq.answer: OpenCode is a coding-agent application that provides the interface and execution workflow. The model used by a session depends on its provider configuration; the application and model service have different responsibilities.

faq.question: Should OpenCode be called a Skill?
faq.answer: No. It is an independent coding-agent project. Skills or other instructions can form part of an agent workflow, but they do not replace the application that runs the workflow.

faq.question: Who publishes the official repository?
faq.answer: The repository is anomalyco/opencode, under Anomaly’s GitHub organization. Community integrations and similarly named projects should be checked separately rather than attributed to Anomaly automatically.

faq.question: Are planning and building the same mode?
faq.answer: The official project documents different agent modes for different responsibilities. Read the selected mode’s behavior and permissions before assuming a planning session can or should make changes.

faq.question: Does MIT include a free model subscription?
faq.answer: No. It covers the application source. Provider accounts, model usage, commercial subscriptions, and external integrations have their own conditions and costs.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use OpenCode as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

Hermes also documents MCP integrations, execution controls, and scheduled tasks. Each connected tool or delivery channel adds its own setup and permissions. The MIT license covers the source, while models, remote systems, and hosted services remain separate choices.

faq.question: How is Hermes Agent different from a Skill collection?
faq.answer: Hermes is the running agent system. Skills are one way it represents reusable task knowledge alongside memory, tools, and scheduling. A collection of instructions alone does not supply that surrounding application.

faq.question: Is persistent memory the same as chat history?
faq.answer: No. The project documents persistent memory and conversation context as distinct concerns. When evaluating it, inspect what is stored, how it is reused, and how you can correct or remove information.

faq.question: Does saving a Skill make it trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. Reusable procedures can contain outdated assumptions or task-specific mistakes. Review their source, dependencies, and results before treating them as a reliable routine.

faq.question: Can Hermes connect to MCP tools?
faq.answer: The official documentation includes MCP integration. The actual services available depend on configured servers, credentials, and access policies; a supported protocol does not grant access to every service.

faq.question: Must I switch products to use these workflow ideas?
faq.answer: No. You can first use Hermes Agent as a reference for task structure, tool boundaries, and result review in your existing workflow. Reusing software is a separate choice that requires compatibility, permissions, and license checks; applying the design ideas does not automatically connect the software to Floatboat.

faq.question: Who maintains Hermes Agent and its source license?

faq.question: ZCode 是否包含 Agent Harness？
faq.answer: 包含。官方将 ZCode 定位为编程 Agent Harness，仓库除应用代码外也包含 Agent CLI 与运行时，并非仅用于展示模型接口的界面。

faq.question: ZCode 只有桌面应用吗？
faq.answer: 不是。仓库介绍桌面、浏览器和终端入口。应分别核对所选入口的要求，不能假设一种入口的配置可以原样应用到另一种。

faq.question: ZCode 官方仓库属于谁？

faq.question: 源码许可覆盖哪些内容？

faq.question: 只看模型能力就能判断 ZCode 效果吗？
faq.answer: 不能。工具配置、上下文组织、执行环境和修改审阅方式都会影响结果，应结合完整任务流程比较，不能以模型名称代替实际效果。

faq.question: 借鉴这些机制是否需要更换工作工具？
faq.answer: 不需要。可以先将 ZCode 作为任务结构、工具边界和结果审阅的设计参考，在已有工作流中验证思路。软件复用是另一项选择，需要核对兼容性、权限与许可；借鉴设计思路不会自动完成软件与 Floatboat 的连接。

en.seoTitle: Ponytail — Coding Agent Skills and Review Workflows | Floatboat
en.description: Ponytail adds reuse-first coding instructions, change review, and repository audits to existing agents. Explore how its rules can reduce unnecessary implementation while keeping tests, security, and accessibility in the workflow.
overview: Ponytail is DietrichGebert’s open-source instruction set for coding agents. Its main Skill and compact AGENTS.md rules ask an agent to understand the affected code before choosing a solution. Existing repository code, standard libraries, platform features, and installed dependencies are considered before a new implementation.

The project also provides change review, repository auditing, and a ledger for deferred shortcuts. Native plugins and instruction-file adapters load the same underlying approach into different hosts, but commands and lifecycle hooks depend on the host. Ponytail supplies working instructions; the host still provides the model, tools, and execution loop.

For work organized in Floatboat, its useful contribution is a concrete method for controlling implementation scope and reviewing consequences beyond a diff. Apply the method to one repository task and compare the result against your acceptance criteria. The project’s own benchmark results are bounded experiments, not guaranteed savings for another model or codebase.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Reuse, Review, and Track Deliberate Shortcuts
en.capabilitiesIntro: Ponytail connects a small implementation with a clear explanation of what was checked, deferred, and affected.

capabilities.title: Inspect before adding code
capabilities.description: Trace the affected flow and look for an existing component, library function, or platform feature before introducing a dependency or abstraction.

capabilities.title: Review the surrounding behavior
capabilities.description: The review examines the change and code it touches; the audit expands that investigation across a repository and prioritizes findings.

capabilities.title: Keep deferred work visible
capabilities.description: Deliberate shortcut comments can be collected into a debt ledger, so a temporary compromise retains a reason and a point for reconsideration.

en.scenariosTitle: Use Ponytail’s Method in Repository Work
en.scenariosIntro: These examples adapt the project’s approach to task design; they do not require replacing your existing workspace.

scenarios.title: Add a form control
scenarios.description: Before building a custom date picker, inspect the project’s input component and native browser support. Validate keyboard interaction and required behavior against the actual form.

scenarios.title: Review a field rename
scenarios.description: Check the callers, serializers, and consumers of the renamed field as well as the diff. A small edit can break an untouched response handler.

scenarios.title: Reduce a sprawling implementation
scenarios.description: Ask which requirements the abstraction serves, remove speculative branches, and keep validation and error handling that protect real inputs.

en.requirementsTitle: Evaluate the Rules in Your Agent Host
en.requirementsIntro: Instruction portability and plugin feature parity are different questions. Check the documented adapter before expecting commands or hooks.

requirements.title: Choose a compatible adapter
requirements.description: Read INSTALL.md for your host. A rules-file adapter loads instructions; a supported plugin can expose commands and lifecycle behavior.

requirements.title: Keep your project contract
requirements.description: Review the rules alongside repository instructions and define the task’s correctness, security, and accessibility requirements before comparing implementations.

requirements.title: Measure a complete result
requirements.description: Compare accepted behavior, changed code, useful tests, and review findings on the same task. Report unverified behavior rather than treating a shorter diff as success.

faq.question: Is Ponytail an autonomous agent or a model?
faq.answer: It is a Skill and plugin project that changes how an existing coding agent approaches work. It does not supply model weights or replace the host’s execution runtime.

faq.question: What is the difference between review and audit?
faq.answer: Review focuses on a change and the surrounding code it affects. Audit investigates the wider repository and orders findings by importance. Neither is simply a request to delete lines.

faq.question: Does every supported host get the same features?
faq.answer: No. Instruction-file adapters can load the rules without plugin commands. Hooks and command syntax depend on the host; check INSTALL.md for that integration.

faq.question: Is the task-cost band available in every agent?
faq.answer: No. The current documentation limits the band to supported Claude Code terminal and desktop environments. Other hosts can use the rules without that interface.

faq.question: Does less code mean skipping safeguards?
faq.answer: No. The project explicitly retains validation, error handling, security, and accessibility. Judge a smaller implementation by whether it meets the same requirements.

faq.question: Are the published benchmark gains guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. They are results from the maintainer’s stated tasks, models, and methodology. Test your own workloads and account for correctness, review effort, and host differences.

zh.seoTitle: Ponytail：编程 Agent Skill、代码复用与审查 | Floatboat
zh.description: Ponytail 为现有编程 Agent 提供优先复用、修改审查与仓库审计规则。了解如何减少不必要的实现，同时保留测试、安全和无障碍要求，为自己的代码工作流明确改动范围与验收标准。
overview: Ponytail 是 DietrichGebert 维护的开源编程指令集。核心 Skill 与精简版 AGENTS.md 要求 Agent 先理解受影响的代码，再选择解决方案：依次检查仓库已有实现、标准库、平台原生能力和已安装依赖，确有需要时才增加新代码。
项目还提供修改审查、整库审计与延期事项台账。不同宿主可通过插件或规则文件加载这套方法，但命令、生命周期钩子和界面能力并不完全相同。Ponytail 负责约束工作方式，模型、工具和执行循环仍由宿主提供。
对在 Floatboat 中组织代码任务的用户，它提供了控制实现范围、检查修改连带影响的方法。可以先选一项仓库任务，按同一验收标准比较结果。项目公布的基准测试有特定任务与模型条件，不能直接当作其他代码库必然节省成本的承诺。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 先复用，再审查，留下有依据的取舍

capabilities.title: 写之前读懂现有实现

capabilities.title: 把审查扩展到关联代码
capabilities.description: 修改审查检查 diff 及其影响的代码，整库审计则扩大调查范围，并按问题的重要程度组织结果。

capabilities.title: 让延期事项可以追踪

scenarios.description: 先查看项目现有 Input 与浏览器日期控件是否满足需求，再决定是否新增日历组件，并核对键盘操作和实际表单行为。

zh.requirementsTitle: 在自己的 Agent 宿主中验证规则

requirements.title: 选择对应适配方式

faq.question: Ponytail 是独立 Agent 或模型吗？
faq.answer: 它是改变现有编程 Agent 工作方式的 Skill 与插件项目，不提供模型权重，也不替代宿主的执行运行时。

faq.question: review 和 audit 有什么区别？
faq.answer: review 围绕一次修改及其关联代码展开，audit 检查更广的仓库范围并排列问题优先级。两者都不只是找可以删除的代码。

faq.question: 不同宿主能使用同样的功能吗？
faq.answer: 不能一概而论。规则文件适配可以加载指令，但不一定带有插件命令；钩子与命令语法也依赖宿主，应查看 INSTALL.md。

faq.question: 任务成本面板可以在所有 Agent 中显示吗？
faq.answer: 不能。当前文档将 band 面板限定于受支持的 Claude Code 终端和桌面环境，其他宿主可以使用规则，但不包含这一界面。

faq.question: 减少代码是否意味着省略安全措施？
faq.answer: 不意味着。项目明确保留验证、错误处理、安全和无障碍要求。更小的实现仍须达到相同的功能与质量标准。

faq.question: 基准测试中的收益可以直接套用吗？
faq.answer: 不可以。那些结果来自维护者公布的任务、模型与测试方法。自己的工作负载仍需核对正确性、审阅成本和宿主差异。

en.seoTitle: MausBot / OpenMausBot — Multi-Agent Workflow Design | Floatboat
en.description: MausBot, published as OpenMausBot, organizes local agent engines as a team of chat contacts. Explore its role-based channels, execution events, and approval flow to design clearer handoffs and reusable team workflows.
overview: MausBot is an open-source desktop application maintained in milind-soni/OpenMausBot. Its README also uses OpenMausBot and records the former OpenGrokBot name. It presents agents as chat contacts, with separate roles, model choices, conversations, and optional computer and application connections.

The interface talks to a local harness server that manages agent processes and converts provider events into a common stream. The documented engines include Claude, Codex, and Grok CLIs. Local transcripts and workspace data do not make every operation offline: model requests, connected services, and cloud computers have their own data paths and access terms.

For a Floatboat workflow, the useful design questions are how to divide responsibility, preserve shared context, and ask for approval at the right point. MausBot’s channels and portable team packages provide concrete examples. Studying that design does not establish an installed integration between the two applications.
en.capabilitiesIntro: The application separates the conversation interface from the engines that carry out work.

capabilities.title: Give a channel its own context
capabilities.description: Channels can define a working folder, shared instructions, bot roster, and responder rules, so several roles can work within one explicit context.

capabilities.title: Normalize engine activity
capabilities.description: A local server owns the agent processes and exposes a common event stream. Tool activity and permission requests can be presented without making every engine’s protocol the user interface.

capabilities.title: Package a repeatable team
capabilities.description: Team files can describe bots, channels, playbooks, and suggested routines. Import review and paused routines separate reusable instructions from live permissions.

en.scenariosTitle: Design Handoffs for a Small Agent Team
en.scenariosIntro: Start with complementary responsibilities and a shared deliverable, rather than adding bots without a division of work.

scenarios.title: Separate research from review
scenarios.description: Have one role collect source material and another check claims against those sources. Define the shared folder and the evidence each handoff must contain.

scenarios.title: Prepare a recurring operations brief
scenarios.description: Specify the schedule, connected information sources, and report format. Keep drafting separate from sending messages or changing external records.

scenarios.title: Reuse an established team playbook
scenarios.description: Distribute roles and instructions as a reviewed package, then reconnect services and approve execution in the receiving environment.

en.requirementsIntro: A bot profile describes the job; engines, service access, and operating-system capabilities determine what can actually run.

requirements.title: Confirm a working agent engine
requirements.description: The desktop setup checks a supported local engine and its account. An open-source application does not include unlimited model access or remove provider limits.

requirements.title: Choose the computer and connections
requirements.description: Local computer use, cloud desktops, and connected applications require different permissions and services. Test the specific path needed by the task.

requirements.title: Check approvals and portable data
requirements.description: Review what the team file contains and which actions require consent. A shared playbook should not be treated as a transfer of credentials or computer access.

faq.question: Are MausBot and OpenMausBot different projects?
faq.answer: The upstream README identifies MausBot as another name for OpenMausBot and records OpenGrokBot as a former name. The canonical source used here is milind-soni/OpenMausBot.

faq.question: Is MausBot a language model?
faq.answer: No. It is an application and local harness around supported agent engines. Bot roles and model choices sit above those engines; inference still depends on the selected provider.

faq.question: Does local-first mean all work stays offline?
faq.answer: No. Local conversations and workspace data coexist with requests to model providers, connected applications, or cloud computers when those features are used. Evaluate each enabled service separately.

faq.question: What makes a channel different from a single bot thread?
faq.answer: A channel can hold shared instructions, a working folder, multiple bots, and responder rules. It defines the context in which those roles collaborate.

faq.question: Can a shared team package carry live credentials?
faq.answer: The documented team-sharing flow excludes keys, passwords, chat history, model choices, and computers. Import behavior differs for organization-managed packages, so inspect the relevant sharing documentation.

faq.question: Is the open-source app the same as free model and cloud access?
faq.answer: No. Apache-2.0 covers the application source. Agent accounts, API usage, connected services, cloud computers, and managed offerings have separate costs and terms.

zh.seoTitle: MausBot / OpenMausBot：多 Agent 工作流设计 | Floatboat
zh.description: MausBot 以 OpenMausBot 发布，将本地 Agent 引擎组织为聊天式团队。了解角色频道、执行事件与人工审批，借鉴共享上下文和团队包的设计，为自己的工作流明确分工、交接与执行环境。
overview: MausBot 是在 milind-soni/OpenMausBot 仓库维护的开源桌面应用。README 同时使用 OpenMausBot 名称，并记录其曾用名 OpenGrokBot。它把 Agent 呈现为聊天联系人，各自拥有角色、模型选择、对话，以及可选的电脑和应用连接。
界面通过本地 harness 服务管理 Agent 进程，将不同供应方的事件转换为统一事件流。文档列出的引擎包括 Claude、Codex 和 Grok CLI。本地保存对话与工作区资料，并不代表所有任务都离线完成；模型请求、外部应用和云电脑仍有各自的数据流向与访问条件。
对 Floatboat 用户，更值得借鉴的是如何划分角色、保留共享上下文，以及在正确的步骤请求审批。MausBot 的频道与可移植团队包提供了具体实现参考；研究这些机制，不代表两个应用之间已经完成安装或集成。

faq.question: MausBot 和 OpenMausBot 是两个项目吗？
faq.answer: 上游 README 将 MausBot 列为 OpenMausBot 的另一名称，并记录 OpenGrokBot 为曾用名。这里采用的原始仓库是 milind-soni/OpenMausBot。

faq.question: MausBot 本身是大语言模型吗？
faq.answer: 不是。它是围绕受支持 Agent 引擎构建的应用与本地 harness。角色与模型选择位于引擎之上，推理仍取决于选用的供应方。

faq.question: 本地优先代表所有任务都不联网吗？
faq.answer: 不代表。本地保存的对话和工作区资料，可以与发往模型供应方、外部应用或云电脑的请求同时存在。需要分别检查实际启用的服务。

faq.question: 频道和单个 bot 对话有什么不同？
faq.answer: 频道可以定义共享指令、工作目录、多个 bot 以及响应规则，为这些角色提供共同的协作背景。

faq.question: 共享团队包会携带真实凭证吗？
faq.answer: 文档中的团队共享流程排除密钥、密码、聊天历史、模型选择和电脑配置。组织管理的导入流程可能不同，应核对对应的共享说明。

faq.question: 开源应用是否包含免费模型和云电脑？
faq.answer: 不包含。Apache-2.0 覆盖应用源码；Agent 账号、API 用量、外部服务、云电脑和托管方案有各自的费用与条款。

en.seoTitle: Agent Desktop by Vercel Labs — Desktop Automation for Agents | Floatboat
en.description: Agent Desktop exposes desktop apps through operating-system accessibility trees. Explore Vercel Labs’ CLI and C library to design observe–act–verify workflows, handle stale element references, and check platform permissions before automating a task.
overview: Agent Desktop is an open-source desktop automation tool from Vercel Labs. Its CLI and C library expose app structure through operating-system accessibility APIs, returning JSON snapshots and references to actionable elements. The calling agent chooses the next step; Agent Desktop supplies observation and control rather than its own planning model.

The core interaction is to inspect a snapshot, act on an element reference, and inspect the result. References belong to their snapshot, so an outdated or ambiguous target calls for renewed observation. Accessibility actions are headless by default; enabling physical input is a separate choice, and exact capabilities differ across operating systems.

For workflows organized in Floatboat, the project provides a reference for desktop steps that need observable targets and explicit verification. Examples include entering prepared data into an application and checking the resulting state. Reusing the tool requires a compatible integration and the necessary permissions; a directory listing does not connect it to Floatboat.
en.capabilitiesTitle: Observe, Act, and Verify Desktop State
en.capabilitiesIntro: A structured target and a successful command are different forms of evidence. Check the resulting application state before continuing.

capabilities.title: Read app structure as JSON
capabilities.description: Snapshots expose roles, labels, windows, and actionable references through native accessibility APIs. This gives the caller a structured view of supported application controls.

capabilities.title: Act on scoped element references
capabilities.description: Clicks and value changes target references from an observed snapshot. Stale or ambiguous references require another snapshot instead of silently retargeting an action.

capabilities.title: Inspect errors before retrying
capabilities.description: Command envelopes describe success or a structured error. The documented retry disposition helps the caller distinguish a safe retry from an action that needs investigation.

en.scenariosTitle: Plan a Desktop Step with a Checkable Result
en.scenariosIntro: Use desktop control for a specific application task and define the visible state that will count as completion.

scenarios.title: Transfer reviewed information into an app
scenarios.description: Prepare and validate the source data first, locate the actual target controls, and inspect the saved values after entry.

scenarios.title: Recover after a list changes
scenarios.description: If an item disappears or the target becomes ambiguous, take another snapshot and locate the intended row again before attempting an action.

scenarios.title: Embed control in an existing runtime
scenarios.description: Compare CLI calls with the C library when your agent already owns task context and planning. Keep approval and verification decisions in that surrounding workflow.

en.requirementsTitle: Check the Platform Before Desktop Automation
en.requirementsIntro: Support for an operating system does not guarantee identical controls, permissions, or screenshot behavior in every environment.

requirements.title: Confirm permissions and session access
requirements.description: macOS requires Accessibility permission. Windows control is constrained by process integrity level; Linux needs an accessible graphical session and the documented platform dependencies.

requirements.title: Check the exact app and display system
requirements.description: Validate the target app’s accessibility exposure. Linux X11 and Wayland differ for input, screenshots, and clipboard operations; read the current platform capability table.

requirements.title: Limit sensitive observation data
requirements.description: Snapshots, clipboard contents, screenshots, and traces can contain private material. Keep the collected evidence scoped to the task and check any optional model-backed helper separately.

faq.question: Is Agent Desktop an agent harness or a model?
faq.answer: It is a tool an agent can invoke, delivered as a CLI and C library. The surrounding agent still owns planning, model calls, approvals, and the decision to continue.

faq.question: How does it differ from Agent Browser?
faq.answer: Agent Desktop targets desktop applications through OS accessibility APIs. Agent Browser focuses on browser automation. Choose the tool according to where the task’s controls actually live.

faq.question: What happens when an element reference becomes stale?
faq.answer: References are scoped to snapshots. On a stale or ambiguous target, observe again and use a reference from the new snapshot rather than assuming the old reference still identifies the intended element.

faq.question: Does headless mean it runs without a graphical environment?
faq.answer: No. Here it means default actions use accessibility APIs without taking focus or moving the pointer. Linux still needs the user’s graphical session, and physical-input capabilities have additional platform conditions.

faq.question: Can all three operating systems perform the same actions?
faq.answer: No. The documentation lists platform-specific differences for mouse input, screenshots, clipboard access, notifications, and system surfaces. Check the current table for the actual environment.

faq.question: Does a Skill installation include desktop permissions?
faq.answer: No. Instructions explain how an agent should use the tool. The executable, its platform helpers, OS permissions, and any host integration remain separate setup requirements.

zh.seoTitle: Vercel Labs Agent Desktop：Agent 桌面自动化工具 | Floatboat
zh.description: Agent Desktop 通过操作系统无障碍树读取并操作桌面应用。了解 Vercel Labs 的 CLI 与 C 库，围绕观察、操作和验证设计桌面工作流，处理失效元素引用，并核对不同平台的权限与能力边界。
zh.overviewTitle: 关于 Vercel Labs Agent Desktop
overview: Agent Desktop 是 Vercel Labs 发布的开源桌面自动化工具，通过 CLI 与 C 库访问操作系统无障碍接口，将应用结构转换为 JSON 快照和可操作元素引用。下一步由调用它的 Agent 决定；工具负责观察与控制，不自带负责规划的模型。
它的核心循环是读取快照、操作元素引用，再次观察结果。引用属于对应快照，目标失效或存在歧义时需要重新观察。默认操作通过无障碍接口执行，不主动抢占焦点；允许物理输入是另一项选择，具体能力也因操作系统而异。
对在 Floatboat 中组织的工作流，它为需要明确目标与结果验证的桌面步骤提供参考，例如把已核对的数据录入应用，再检查保存后的状态。实际复用仍需兼容的集成方式与必要权限，目录收录不会自动将这一工具接入 Floatboat。
zh.capabilitiesTitle: 观察桌面状态，操作后再次验证
zh.capabilitiesIntro: 明确的元素目标与命令执行成功是两种不同证据，继续下一步前还应检查应用实际状态。

capabilities.title: 把应用结构转为 JSON
capabilities.description: 快照通过原生无障碍接口返回角色、标签、窗口与可操作引用，为调用方提供受支持控件的结构化视图。

capabilities.title: 按快照中的元素引用操作
capabilities.description: 点击和赋值指向已观察的元素引用；目标过期或无法唯一确定时，需要重新取快照，而不是悄悄换一个目标继续。

capabilities.title: 先理解错误再决定重试
capabilities.description: 命令返回统一结果与结构化错误；重试标记帮助调用方判断可以安全重复，还是必须先调查当前状态。

zh.scenariosTitle: 为桌面步骤定义可检查的结果
zh.scenariosIntro: 围绕一个明确的应用任务使用桌面控制，先约定什么可见状态才算完成。

scenarios.title: 把已核对资料录入应用
scenarios.description: 先准备并验证输入，再定位真实控件，录入后检查保存的值，让数据准备与界面操作各有验收依据。

scenarios.title: 在列表变化后恢复操作
scenarios.description: 条目消失或目标不明确时，重新读取快照并定位预期行，再决定是否执行，避免把动作落到相邻条目。

scenarios.title: 为既有运行层补充桌面能力
scenarios.description: 当自己的 Agent 已掌握任务背景与规划时，比较 CLI 调用和 C 库接入，将审批与结果验证保留在外围工作流中。

zh.requirementsTitle: 桌面自动化前先核对运行平台
zh.requirementsIntro: 支持某个操作系统，不代表所有环境都有相同的控件、权限或截图行为。

requirements.title: 确认权限与会话条件
requirements.description: macOS 需要无障碍权限；Windows 操作受进程完整性级别限制；Linux 需要可访问的图形会话及文档要求的平台依赖。

requirements.title: 核对应用与显示系统
requirements.description: 先验证目标应用是否暴露需要的无障碍控件。Linux 的 X11 与 Wayland 在输入、截图和剪贴板方面存在差异，应查看当前平台能力表。

requirements.title: 控制观察资料的范围
requirements.description: 快照、剪贴板、截图与跟踪记录可能包含私人资料，应只采集任务所需证据，并单独检查可选模型辅助功能的数据流向。

faq.question: Agent Desktop 是 Agent Harness 或模型吗？
faq.answer: 它是可由 Agent 调用的工具，以 CLI 和 C 库交付。规划、模型请求、审批以及是否继续执行，仍由外围 Agent 与工作流负责。

faq.question: 它和 Agent Browser 有什么区别？
faq.answer: Agent Desktop 通过操作系统无障碍接口操作桌面应用；Agent Browser 主要面向浏览器自动化。应根据任务控件实际所在的环境选择。

faq.question: 元素引用失效时应该怎么办？
faq.answer: 引用受对应快照约束。目标过期或存在歧义时，应重新观察并使用新快照中的引用，不能假定旧引用仍指向原来的元素。

faq.question: 默认 headless 是否代表不需要图形环境？
faq.answer: 不是。这里指默认通过无障碍接口操作，不抢占焦点或移动鼠标。Linux 仍需要用户图形会话，物理输入还受额外平台条件限制。

faq.question: 三个操作系统的能力完全相同吗？
faq.answer: 不相同。文档分别说明鼠标输入、截图、剪贴板、通知与系统面板等差异，需要针对实际运行环境核对当前能力表。

faq.question: 安装 Skill 就拥有桌面操作权限了吗？
faq.answer: 没有。Skill 说明 Agent 应如何使用工具；可执行程序、平台辅助文件、操作系统权限与宿主集成仍是独立的准备条件。
